name: Sheng-to-Sanifu Code-Switching Semantic Lexicon
description: An open-source linguistic mapping dataset bridging Sheng (Kenyan Urban Youth Vernacular & Code-Switching) to Standard Kiswahili (Sanifu) and English, with morphological breakdowns for NLP tokenization.

morphology.prefix_function: Swahili Bantu plural marker for Class 5/6

usage_examples.sheng: Niko mtaani na mayouth.
usage_examples.swahili: Niko mtaani pamoja na vijana.
usage_examples.english: I am in the hood with the youths.

usage_examples.sheng: Mayouth wa mtaa wanatafuta hustle.
usage_examples.swahili: Vijana wa mtaani wanatafuta kazi au biashara.
usage_examples.english: The neighborhood youths are looking for hustles.

entries.english: in the hood / in the neighborhood / at home

usage_examples.sheng: Rada ya mtaani ikoje leo?
usage_examples.swahili: Hali ya mtaani ikoje leo?
usage_examples.english: How is the situation in the hood today?

morphology.function: fashionable attire / sharp visual style / drip

entries.standard_swahili: mavazi nadhifu / mtindo maridadi wa mavazi

morphology.kutendesha: shikisha -> pass fire / light up (e.g. nishikishe kiberiti niwashe fegi)

entries.standard_swahili: washa sigara / patia moto / nunulia kinywaji
entries.english: light up / pass fire / (applicative) buy a drink for someone

morphology.meaning: I am aware / I'm good / I'm alert

morphology.etymology: Derived from English 'dough' (money), adapted to Sheng open-syllable phonology

usage_examples.english: Yesterday was when he was fired, right now he has no money.

morphology.phonological_process: Vowel elision: English silent 'e' dropped before Bantu passive suffix '-iwa'

usage_examples.sheng: Alifiriwa jana na boss kwa ofisi bila notice.
usage_examples.swahili: Alifutwa kazi jana na mkuu katika ofisi bila taarifa.
usage_examples.english: He was fired yesterday by the boss at the office without notice.

entries.english: send to me / forward / throw to me (link or money)

usage_examples.english: Send/forward me that application link on WhatsApp.

morphology.etymology: Derived from popular street dance culture and Congolese rhumba influence (Kasongo / kusonga), meaning to dance or groove rhythmically on stage or in club settings

usage_examples.swahili: Huyo mtu alicheza muziki na askari jukwaani.
usage_examples.english: That guy danced with the police officer on stage.
